analysis:
This PR adds a dense-Qwen 'demanded latest' checkpoint partition. The new EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens (EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift head 61-79) returns the store floor only when four conditions hold: backend == .paged, isDenseQwen35(model), the store is an SSDHybridCheckpointStore, and its backendLayout is pagedLayout or nativeQuantizedPagedLayout. Otherwise it returns nil, which leaves the cut disabled. The docs (prefix-cache.md head 670-690) describe one extra range ending at least 64 tokens below the prompt end. The cut boundary becomes the rolling latest. Fleet-novel refusal, the first/target/latest retention limits and the byte/staging caps are stated as unchanged.

T-041 assessment: this changes prefill partitioning and which aligned boundaries are captured. It does not change at-rest crypto, HMAC naming, cacheSalt scoping, TTL, disk budget or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate. Write admission (SSDCheckpointDemand) still gates disk writes. A boundary closer to the prompt end slightly widens reusable prefix coverage, but only within the same authenticated scope. That stays inside the accepted SEC-035 same-account timing residual, so it is not a new exposure. Correctness relies on the documented dense-Qwen partition-invariance (parity report). The provider side restricts the cut to dense Qwen, so MoE and GLM are excluded.

Submodule bump: libs/mlx-swift-lm moves aee6ebb -> 76ff231. The native implementation of demandedLatestCheckpointRange, the scheduler config, and any other native changes in the bump were not supplied. Their bounds, reservation accounting, packing exclusion and the 64-token margin math could not be verified. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. Integration should confirm that the submodule diff contains no changes to SSD crypto, scope or reservation release paths.
